newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabena sees 1996 loss at 3 to 4 bln Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabena sees 1996 loss at 3 to 4 bln Bfr.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena is heading for a 1996 full year loss of between three and four billion francs ($88.2 and $117.6 million), a senior offical was quoted on Thursday as saying.

Patrick du Bois, who holds the post of Secretary-General and is the chief assistant to chief executive Paul Reutlinger, told De Standaard newspaper in an interview that the real test for Sabena would be an assessment after the first half of 1997 made by dominant shareholder Swissair.
"The pressure of Swissair exists, that is no secret, certainly now that our loss for 1996 could be between three and four billion francs," said du Bois.
He added that 1997 should still see a slight loss "but the Swiss are taking this into account.This will be a year of transition". "In 1998 we need to make profit again," he added.
Du Bois, who is also Sabena executive vice-president, was not available for comment and the carrier's spokesman declined to comment.

Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs ($15.6 million) and a two billion franc ($58.8 million) net loss in the first half of 1996.
Media reports had earlier estimated the full-year 1996 loss could be between four and six billion francs ($117.6 and 176.5 million).
